subject.title: Unhandled socket error in SSRF fetch wrapper can kill the gateway process (IPv6-only DNS + Happy Eyeballs)

question: Should this issue be fixed by repairing the open linked socket-error PR, or should maintainers fold it into the broader guarded-fetch family-selection work tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87763?
rationale: The core bug is valid, but the repair touches SSRF DNS pinning and the current linked PR has unresolved security-boundary/proof concerns, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary shape.

options.title: Repair the linked PR
options.body: Keep this issue paired with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100433, require the PR to preserve explicit-proxy pinning and add live or log proof, then close after merge.

options.title: Fold into broader guarded-fetch work
options.body: Close or supersede the linked PR only after a broader fix under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87763 covers this IPv6-only crash path with proof.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Leave the issue open and request an IPv6-unreachable Docker/Linux reproduction before accepting any security-boundary patch.

recommendation.title: Repair the linked PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue paired with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100433, require the PR to preserve explicit-proxy pinning and add live or log proof, then close after merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Current central-code blame and prior network-boundary review context make this the best available owner for the security-boundary choice.
